Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then apply the required fish-control transfer protocol and inspect both wake visual views before touching the policy. I’ll keep the candidate-specific rationale in the requested notes and only promote evidence-backed lessons into reusable guidance.

The workspace requires a pre-edit diagnosis and forbids local CFD. I’m now consulting the fish-control bookshelf because this is the first architecture proposal from the seed; I’m also using the visual-signals-first skill so the diagnosis is grounded in both rendered wake views, not metrics alone.

The inherited notes show the prior worker proposed the first same-sign posterior C-bend, so its completed rollout is the key new evidence this iteration must distill. I’m treating the best sampled `3.691L` trajectory as the finite baseline and that completed C-bend rollout as the mechanism test; both report direct-uniform still water.

The visual comparison is decisive: the C-bend preserves the approach and wake through `20T`, realizes the requested same-sign posterior mean afterward, and produces stronger late yaw—but it curls toward a rear-facing state and exits sooner instead of reducing target error. That falsifies “same-sign curvature” as sufficient and points to closed-loop yaw-direction/load feedback, not another bend-amplitude tweak. I’m now consulting the bookshelf references to choose one genuinely distinct mechanism and its falsification test.

The bookshelf transfer I’m adopting is posterior reactive-load steering: preserve the evidenced traveling carrier, but use a bounded, target-gated posterior mean deflection whose sign is calibrated from the completed rollout’s yaw response. The prior same-sign C-bend is the falsifier—its posterior mean changed as intended, but yaw and target error changed the wrong way. I’ll record that diagnosis before editing, as required.

The policy edit will preserve the inherited oscillator and phase-selective carrier, while replacing the failed late C-bend with one earlier, smoothly scheduled posterior counter-deflection. It is zero at long range/alignment, uses only normalized distance and body-frame target geometry, and keeps all active values in `target_policy_params()`.

I’m now promoting the durable result into guidance: the prior C-bend was not merely “insufficient”—it successfully changed posterior geometry and thereby calibrated the yaw sign, which rules out geometric same-sign assumptions. I’m also recording the one-sided envelope’s smaller alignment improvement as a bounded positive result, without claiming evidence for the new candidate.

The candidate and reusable guidance are both updated. Per the workspace contract, I’m invoking the dedicated check runner now; it will perform only the guidance-delta, lightweight Julia contract, and editable-boundary checks—no CFD.

The configured check-runner model is unavailable in this environment, so the invocation itself failed before running commands. I’m executing the three prescribed checks directly and separately, preserving the same no-CFD boundary.

The first check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` lists the same assigned guidance parent twice with the “copied to guidance” marker, while the validator requires exactly one marker. I’ll remove only that duplicate listing, then rerun the prescribed check; this does not alter solver behavior or evidence.

All three prescribed checks now pass after repairing the duplicate parent marker. I corrected the notes to match the implemented `8L → 5.5L` smooth recruitment schedule and am doing one final lightweight consistency pass on the notes delta, parameter schema, and reflection symmetry.

Produced exactly one candidate: a target-gated posterior reactive-rudder policy that preserves the traveling carrier while reversing the failed C-bend’s measured yaw sign.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:23)

The bookshelf informed the posterior reactive-load invariant; no published gains or routes were transferred. All prescribed guidance, Julia contract, parameter-schema, reflection-symmetry, and boundary checks pass. No CFD was run. I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that initially prevented the required guidance validator from running.
